versions.intended: English for everyone outside the UK, prices in USD
English for the United Kingdom, prices in GBP with VAT
German for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, prices in EUR

summary: Set health is 0 of 6 clusters: one invalid code ('en-uk') in the root template breaks the UK pairing on every checked page, worth 50,830 impressions in 28 days.
In the UK, 58.2% of impressions on these pages go to a version not meant for the UK (fail). On pricing, Google has folded /uk/pricing/ into /pricing/.

France is the next market: 4.1% of impressions already, at position 31.5 on English pages, and French searches add up to 52.3% of the US total. Spain is a watch: 25.7% size ratio but 2.0% of impressions and no Spanish support yet.
Add France as a subfolder, /fr/, with the language-only code 'fr': 4 of 10 top results for the largest French term are on .fr domains, and there is no French entity or team.

markets.why: already has a version; sized so its keyword list can be mapped

markets.business_readiness: French support in place and EUR billing
markets.why: size ratio 52.3% (25% needed) and 4.1% of impressions (3% needed), and the business can sell and support there
size ratio 25.7% meets 25%, but 2.0% of impressions is under 3%, and no Spanish-speaking support yet

new_version.serves: France, plus French speakers in Belgium and Switzerland

why: One company, one team, one website; no local entity in France or Spain (one company, registered in the US; no local entities).
Local SERPs: 4 of 10 .fr results in France and 3 of 10 .es results in Spain, under the 7 of 10 that would favour a country domain; 3 global sites rank from a French subfolder.
French pricing is the same EUR price as the German version, so a language-only code covers every French-speaking market. Add fr-ch only if CHF pricing launches.

code_changes.why: the root serves every English searcher outside the UK, and Australia sends 21.7% of these impressions to /uk/ today
'uk' is not a region code; Google ignores the tag

bing.recommend: In Bing Webmaster, set /uk/ to United Kingdom. Leave /de/ and the future /fr/ unset: they serve several countries.

gate.title: Online booking software for small businesses

issues.fix: In the root template, change 'en-uk' to 'en-gb'. One template line fixes all 6 clusters.
Add the en-gb alternate to the /de/ salons and blog templates, so both pairs link back.
Set the canonical on /de/preise/ to itself.

rows.cause: the root pages label the UK version 'en-uk', an invalid code, so the root/UK pair carries no country signal; and Google picked /pricing/ as the canonical of /uk/pricing/
the root says 'en-us', so Australian searchers match no English version exactly and some land on /uk/; labelling the root 'en' makes it the match for every English searcher outside the UK
Switzerland has French and Italian speakers too; part of this is English searching on purpose, so treat it as a watch item

url_inspection.coverage_state: Duplicate, Google chose different canonical than user

worst.reading: Google treats /uk/pricing/ as a duplicate of /pricing/ and shows the US page in the UK. Fix the code, then make the UK page differ for real: GBP prices with VAT, UK payment methods and UK customer examples.

fr_release_check: body translated by a French writer, not machine output in a French template
only then added to every cluster's hreflang set

rollout: Week 1: fix the root template code ('en-uk' to 'en-gb', root 'en-us' to 'en'), add x-default to /uk/, add the missing en-gb links on the /de/ salons and blog templates, set the /de/preise/ canonical to itself, and set lang="de" on /de/funktionen/erinnerungen/ once its body is confirmed German.
Week 1: rewrite /uk/pricing/ with GBP prices including VAT and UK examples, so it differs from /pricing/; publish the international sitemap.
Weeks 2 to 6: brief a French writer from the FR keyword list (copywriting handoff), build the 7 French pages, and run the release check on each.
After launch: rerun this skill on the 28 days after the fixes; the UK wrong-version share should fall under 20%.
unknowns: The crawler reads tags, not body language: check that /de/funktionen/erinnerungen/ is written in German.
Spain's readiness is a business call: Spanish-speaking support decides when it moves from watch to serve next.
